title: Quant & Graduate Theory
intro: This level covers no-arbitrage pricing, the Greeks, risk-neutral valuation, Brownian motion and Ito's lemma, asset-pricing theory, financial econometrics and measure-theoretic probability. It also covers the choice and checking of numerical methods for exotic and structured products, without coding.

modules.title: Derivatives pricing & Greeks
modules.hook: Binomial trees, no-arbitrage pricing, Black-Scholes, put-call parity and the Greeks, applied to the pricing of a capital-protected note.

units.title: No-arbitrage and the forward price
objectives: Explain arbitrage and the law of one price in a worked example
Compute a forward price with cash-and-carry, including discrete dividends
Use put-call parity to price a put from a call and to spot a violation
units.worked_example: Spot 100 EUR, 1y rate 3% cont., dividend 2 EUR in 6 months: F = (100 - 2e^-0.015)e^0.03; a quoted forward 3 EUR higher is an arbitrage you can construct leg by leg.

exercises.task: Compute the fair forward price for a stock with a known dividend
exercises.params: spot, rate, dividend size and date, maturity

exercises.task: Sequence the legs of a cash-and-carry arbitrage when the forward is too rich
Use put-call parity to find the European put price
exercises.params: call price, strike, rate, maturity, dividend

exercises.task: Spot the error in a dealer's option quote sheet that breaks a no-arbitrage bound
exercises.params: which bound is broken: intrinsic, parity, monotonicity

exercises.task: Which position replicates a long forward?

sources.ref: Ch. 5 (forward prices), Ch. 11 (properties of stock options)

units.title: One-period binomial model: replication and risk-neutral pricing
objectives: Replicate a call with stock and cash in a one-step tree and derive its price
Compute risk-neutral probabilities and show they are not real-world probabilities
Explain why the real-world up-probability does not enter the option price

exercises.task: Solve for the delta and bond holding that replicate the payoff
Compute q and the option price as discounted expectation; check against the replication cost
If the real-world probability of an up-move rises, what happens to the call price?
exercises.params: stated probabilities, answer is always 'no change'

exercises.task: Fill in the no-arbitrage condition on u, d and the gross rate
Spot why a given tree admits arbitrage (d >= R or u <= R)

units.title: Multi-period trees (CRR) and American options
objectives: Build a two- and three-step CRR tree and price a European option by backward induction
Decide early exercise node by node for an American put
Calibrate u, d to a volatility and explain why dividends change the early-exercise logic for calls
units.worked_example: Three-step tree, S0 = 50, sigma = 30%, T = 6m, r = 3%: u = 1.130; an American put at strike 55 is exercised early at the lowest nodes, so its value exceeds the European put by a small early-exercise premium.

exercises.task: Complete a 3-step price tree and option-value tree
exercises.params: S0, u, d, r, strike, call/put

exercises.task: Compute u, d and q from volatility, rate and step length
Sort nodes into 'exercise now' vs 'hold' for an American put
When is early exercise of an American call on a non-dividend stock optimal?
Delta at each node: read the hedge ratio off the tree

units.title: From the tree to Black-Scholes: lognormal prices and the formula
objectives: Explain how a many-step tree converges to lognormal stock prices
Compute a European call and put with the Black-Scholes formula using N(d1), N(d2)
Interpret N(d2) as risk-neutral exercise probability and N(d1) as delta of the call
units.worked_example: S = 100, K = 100, r = 2%, sigma = 25%, T = 1: d1 = 0.205, d2 = -0.045, call about 10.9 EUR; N(d2) about 0.48 is the risk-neutral probability of finishing in the money.

exercises.task: Compute d1, d2 and the call price
exercises.params: S, K, r, sigma, T, dividend yield

exercises.task: Price the put via put-call parity and check against the direct formula
Which parameters of the stock process does the formula NOT depend on?
Match each term of the formula to its economic meaning
exercises.params: terms: S N(d1), K e^{-rT} N(d2), d1, d2

exercises.task: Write a half page explaining to a client why two analysts with different return forecasts agree on the same option price
exercises.params: optional self-graded; rubric covers replication argument

units.title: The Black-Scholes PDE and risk-neutral valuation
objectives: State the Black-Scholes PDE and identify each term (theta, delta, gamma, financing)
Explain why the delta-hedged portfolio earns the risk-free rate
Describe, without full proof, how the PDE and the discounted-expectation formula are two views of the same price
key_concepts: assumptions of BS and their failures
units.worked_example: For an at-the-money option with gamma 0.02 per EUR^2, sigma 25% and S = 100, theta is roughly -0.5 x 0.0625 x 10,000 x 0.02 = -6.25 EUR/year per option: time decay pays for gamma.

exercises.task: Use theta ~ -0.5 sigma^2 S^2 gamma (r = 0 case) to estimate daily decay from gamma
Order the steps of the hedging argument that leads to the PDE
Sort assumptions into 'holds in practice' vs 'breaks': continuous trading, constant vol, no jumps, no costs
Fill in the PDE with theta, delta, gamma and r terms
Which function solves the PDE with the payoff max(S-K,0) as terminal condition?

sources.ref: Ch. 15 (derivation of the differential equation), Appendix on Ito

units.title: The Greeks: definitions, signs and shapes
objectives: Define delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho and sketch each versus spot for calls and puts
Compute Greeks of a position from per-option Greeks and quantity
Explain the delta-gamma-theta Taylor approximation of option P&L
units.worked_example: Short 100 calls (multiplier 100): delta per call 0.55, gamma 0.03; a 2 EUR spot rise costs about 100 x 100 x (0.55 x 2 + 0.5 x 0.03 x 4) = 11,600 EUR before hedging.

exercises.task: Compute portfolio delta and gamma of a multi-option position
Estimate P&L of a spot move using delta-gamma Taylor
Match each Greek to its chart shape (bell, S-curve, monotone)
Which Greek of an at-the-money option is largest just before expiry?
Sort positions as long gamma / short gamma

units.title: Greeks in practice: hedging P&L, implied volatility, smile and skew
objectives: Explain delta-hedging P&L as realised vs implied variance times gamma
Back out the direction of implied vol from quoted option prices (conceptually, no solver)
Describe the smile/skew and why equity skew is negative
units.worked_example: A desk delta-hedges a long 25%-implied option daily while stock realises 30%: gain about 0.5 x gamma x S^2 x (0.30^2 - 0.25^2)/252 per day, positive despite theta.

exercises.task: Compute daily hedged P&L from gamma, realised and implied variance
Skew steepens after a market drop: which strike's implied vol moves most?
Complete a table of daily hedged P&L over 5 days given spot moves
Match market phenomena to smile features (leverage effect, jump fear, supply/demand)
Spot the inconsistency in a quoted vol surface (calendar or butterfly arbitrage)

units.title: Beyond vanilla: exotics, stochastic volatility and structured-product pricing
objectives: Decompose an EU capital-protected note into a zero-coupon bond plus options and price it
Explain barriers, digitals, autocallables and their Greeks, especially discontinuity risk
Contrast local vol, stochastic vol and jump models at the level of what each fixes
key_concepts: issuer funding spread vs option price
units.worked_example: 3-year 100% capital-protected note, 3y zero at 2.9% costs 91.8; remaining 8.2 EUR buys the call, so participation = 8.2 / call price (e.g., 14.2) = about 58%.

exercises.task: Solve participation rate of a capital-protected note from rates and option cost
Approximate a digital with a tight call spread and give its payoff and delta
Sort features into 'hedgeable statically' vs 'needs dynamic hedging'
Why does an autocallable's delta jump near the barrier date, and what does the issuer do?
Optional: explain to a colleague how a model can price a note correctly at inception and still mis-hedge it

sources.ref: Chs. on barrier and autocallable structures

minigame.name: Dealer Desk
minigame.variant: Delta-hedge a small option book as spot and vol move; track hedged P&L vs gamma/theta/vega

modules.unit_test: Replication, tree and BS pricing, put-call parity, Greeks of a position, structured-note decomposition.

modules.title: Stochastic processes & Itô calculus
modules.hook: Random walks, Brownian motion, quadratic variation, Ito's lemma and the change to the risk-neutral measure.

units.title: Random walks and the scaled walk
objectives: Compute mean, variance and distribution of a symmetric random walk after n steps
Explain scaling: why time step dt pairs with step size sqrt(dt)
Describe the central-limit view of the walk converging to a normal
units.worked_example: Walk with step +/-1 per day for 100 days: sd = 10; scale step to sigma sqrt(dt) with sigma = 20% and dt = 1/252 and a year's sd becomes 20%.

exercises.task: Compute mean and sd of an n-step walk
Rescale a daily vol to annual and vice versa
Doubling the horizon multiplies the sd by what?
exercises.params: factors with sqrt(2) as the right answer

exercises.task: Fill in the scaling that keeps variance finite as dt -> 0

units.title: Brownian motion: definition and properties
objectives: State the four defining properties of standard Brownian motion
Compute probabilities of events about W(t) using increments and the normal distribution
Explain why paths are continuous but nowhere differentiable, in words
key_concepts: drift and scale: mu t + sigma W(t)

exercises.task: Probability that W(t) exceeds a level
Covariance and correlation of W(s) and W(t)
Select which processes are Brownian motion
Distribution of X(t) = mu t + sigma W(t) at a horizon

sources.ref: Ch. 3-4 (scaled random walk and Brownian motion)

units.title: Quadratic variation: why ordinary calculus fails
objectives: Compute the quadratic variation of a Brownian path and of a smooth path
Use the rule (dW)^2 = dt, dt dW = 0, (dt)^2 = 0 mechanically
Explain in a sentence why this produces the extra term in Itô's formula
units.worked_example: Daily log returns with sd 1.26% across 252 days give realised QV 252 x 0.0126^2 = 0.040, i.e. annualised vol 20%: the sum of squares converges, the sum of absolute values grows with finer sampling.

exercises.task: Realised variance and vol from a series of 10 returns
Which process has non-zero quadratic variation?
exercises.params: smooth, BM, BM + drift, jump with finite activity

exercises.task: Complete a differential multiplication table
Why QV is independent of drift: compute QV of mu t + sigma W

units.title: The Itô integral: building stochastic integrals
objectives: Describe the Itô integral as the limit of sums with left-endpoint evaluation
State mean-zero and Itô isometry and compute variance of simple integrals
Explain in words why the integral of W dW is (W^2 - t)/2 and not W^2/2
units.worked_example: The integral of W dW from 0 to T: the extra -T/2 is exactly the quadratic-variation correction; E[integral] = 0 consistent with E[W^2 - T] = 0.

exercises.task: Compute variance of the integral of c dW or of t dW with Itô isometry
Why must the integrand be evaluated at the left endpoint?
exercises.params: trading-strategy interpretation: cannot see the future

exercises.task: Fill in properties: mean, isometry, martingale
Expected value and variance of a discretised trading gain from holding delta_i over each step

units.title: Itô's lemma: the chain rule for diffusions
objectives: Apply Itô's lemma to functions of W and of t and W
Derive the SDE of S^2, ln S and 1/S given dS = mu S dt + sigma S dW
Explain the -sigma^2/2 correction in the log
key_concepts: Itô's formula f_t dt + f_x dX + 1/2 f_xx (dX)^2
units.worked_example: For f = ln S: d ln S = (mu - sigma^2/2)dt + sigma dW; with mu = 8% and sigma = 20% the median grows at 6%, not 8%.

exercises.task: Compute the drift of ln S, S^2 or sqrt(S) from mu and sigma
Order the mechanical steps of an Itô computation
Tabulate f_t, f_x, f_xx then assemble drift and diffusion for f(S)
Spot the error in a derivation that uses ordinary chain rule
Why is the median of S(T) below its mean?

units.title: Geometric Brownian motion and solving SDEs
objectives: Solve the GBM SDE explicitly and read off moments and quantiles of S(T)
Simulate (conceptually) a path with the exact log-step
Compare arithmetic and geometric returns in a continuous-time setting
key_concepts: lognormal moments E[S] = S0 e^{mu T}
units.worked_example: S0 = 100, mu = 8%, sigma = 20%, T = 5: E[S] = 149.2, median = 100 e^{0.06x5} = 134.9, 5% quantile of the log-return distribution via z = -1.645.

exercises.task: Mean, median and 95% interval of S(T)
Probability the stock ends above a threshold at T
Volatility drag: difference between arithmetic and geometric average growth
Which discretisation preserves positivity of S?

units.title: Mean reversion and other SDEs: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, CIR, Vasicek
objectives: Write and interpret OU / Vasicek / CIR dynamics and their long-run behaviour
Compute conditional mean and variance for an OU process
Link the PDE (Feynman-Kac) and expectation views conceptually
key_concepts: short-rate models as inputs for F4
units.worked_example: Vasicek with a = 0.5, b = 3%, sigma = 1%: after 2 years the expected rate from r0 = 1% is 3% - 2% e^{-1} = 2.26%, and the stationary sd is 1%/sqrt(1) = 1%.

exercises.task: Conditional mean at horizon t for OU/Vasicek
Stationary variance sigma^2 / 2a
Match models to features: GBM, OU, CIR, jump-diffusion
Sort quantities into 'can go negative' vs 'cannot'

units.title: Girsanov, risk-neutral measure and the martingale representation
objectives: State what changing measure does to drift and not to volatility
Derive the risk-neutral dynamics of a stock from the real-world ones
Explain the roles of Girsanov and martingale representation in completeness of Black-Scholes
key_concepts: market price of risk theta = (mu - r)/sigma
units.worked_example: mu = 9%, r = 2%, sigma = 20%: theta = 0.35; under Q the stock drifts at r; same volatility, so vol is observable while mu is not needed for pricing.

exercises.task: Market price of risk and Sharpe ratio from mu, r, sigma
Fill in the risk-neutral SDE
What is invariant under change of measure?
Optional: explain Girsanov to a trader in terms of re-weighting scenarios
exercises.params: rubric: Radon-Nikodym, drift shift, vol unchanged

modules.unit_test: Brownian properties, quadratic variation, Itô's lemma computations, GBM/OU moments, Girsanov in words.

modules.title: Asset pricing theory
modules.hook: Stochastic discount factors, the consumption-based first-order condition, and the derivation of the CAPM and factor models from it.

units.title: Preferences, utility and risk aversion
objectives: Compute expected utility and certainty equivalent for a lottery under CRRA and CARA
Derive absolute and relative risk aversion for given utility functions
Link risk aversion to the required premium for a risky asset
units.worked_example: Log utility, 50/50 gamble on wealth 80 or 120 EUR: EU = 0.5 ln 80 + 0.5 ln 120 = 4.5847, certainty equivalent 97.98 < 100, risk premium about 2.0 EUR.

exercises.task: Certainty equivalent of a gamble under power utility
Relative risk aversion from derivatives u', u'' (calculus drill)
Which preference ranking holds as gamma rises?
Match utility functions to CRRA/CARA/neither

units.title: The fundamental equation: stochastic discount factor
objectives: Derive price = E[m x] from a two-period investor problem
Use the SDF to price a bond, a stock and a zero-cost excess return
Decompose the risk premium into -cov(m, R)
units.worked_example: m takes 1.1 in a bad state (p = 0.4) and 0.7 in a good state (p = 0.6); E[m] = 0.86 so Rf = 16.3%; a payoff paying 100 in the bad state only is worth 44 EUR.

exercises.task: Price a payoff given state probabilities and SDF values
Risk premium from cov(m, R)
Sequence the steps of the derivation from investor FOC to price
Why is an asset positively correlated with consumption growth risky?
Complete a state-price table: probability, m, payoff, contribution

units.title: SDF, beta pricing and the Hansen-Jagannathan bound
objectives: Show that any beta-pricing model corresponds to an SDF linear in factors
Use the Hansen-Jagannathan bound to bound the SDF volatility from Sharpe ratios
Compare CAPM and mean-variance frontiers in SDF language
units.worked_example: Equity Sharpe ratio 0.4: sigma(m)/E(m) must be at least 0.4. With CRRA = 2 and consumption growth vol 1.5%, sigma(m) is only about 3%, a large gap.

exercises.task: Minimum SDF volatility implied by a Sharpe ratio
Convert a CAPM beta and market premium into an SDF coefficient b
A model with higher sigma(m) than the bound implies what for prices?
Match each model (CAPM, CCAPM, APT) to its SDF form

sources.ref: Ch. 5-6 (beta representations, mean-variance frontier), Ch. 4.5 (HJ bound)

units.title: Consumption-based asset pricing and the equity premium puzzle
objectives: Compute equity premium implied by CRRA preferences and consumption growth
State the Mehra-Prescott puzzle and the risk-free rate puzzle
List the main directions out of the puzzles
units.worked_example: Historical premium 6%, consumption-growth vol 1.5%, correlation with stock 0.2, stock vol 16%: gamma = 6% / (0.2 x 1.5% x 16%) = 125, implausibly high.

exercises.task: Compute implied gamma from premium and covariance
Why is the risk-free rate puzzle related to the equity premium puzzle?
Sort proposed resolutions: preferences / market frictions / beliefs / data
Implied risk-free rate in a model with high gamma and growth

units.title: Recursive preferences, habits and long-run risk
objectives: Distinguish risk aversion from elasticity of intertemporal substitution (Epstein-Zin)
Explain why habit makes marginal utility counter-cyclical and raises risk premia
Evaluate the empirical realism of each approach
units.worked_example: With gamma = 10 and EIS = 1.5 the model can fit a premium of about 5-6% using persistent expected-growth shocks, unlike CRRA where gamma = 1/EIS.

exercises.task: Match each mechanism to the puzzle it targets
In CRRA, how are EIS and gamma related?
Surplus consumption ratio dynamics, one-step update
Optional: 300 words on which extension is most convincing and why

units.title: Factor models, APT and testing: Fama-French, Fama-MacBeth, GMM
objectives: Explain APT and the link between factor loadings and expected returns
Describe the two-pass Fama-MacBeth regression and what it estimates
Interpret GMM moment conditions E[m R^e] = 0 and pricing-error tests
units.worked_example: Three-factor regression of fund returns gives alpha = 0.25%/month, t = 1.1: significant only if t > 2; with 300 candidate factors some will clear t > 2 by chance.

exercises.task: Expected return from betas and factor premia
t-statistic of an alpha estimate
Order the steps of Fama-MacBeth
Which test statistic uses moment conditions for pricing errors?
Spot the error in a back-tested factor claim

units.title: Complete markets, state prices and the fundamental theorems
objectives: State the two fundamental theorems of asset pricing in finite-state markets
Find state prices by solving a linear system (Arrow securities)
Link SDF, risk-neutral measure and no-arbitrage through the same vector
key_concepts: FTAP I: no arbitrage <-> positive SDF/EMM
units.worked_example: Two assets, three states: bond pays (1,1,1) at price 0.95, stock (80,100,130) at 97: a third security is needed to pin down state prices uniquely; incompleteness yields price intervals for a new payoff.

exercises.task: Solve for state prices from asset prices and payoffs
Which condition guarantees uniqueness of the risk-neutral measure?
Recover m from q and p
Spot the arbitrage in a three-asset price table
Match each statement to FTAP I or II

modules.unit_test: SDF, HJ bound, CCAPM puzzles, factor model tests, state prices and FTAP.

modules.title: Financial econometrics
modules.hook: Time-series models, stationarity, volatility estimation (GARCH), regression pitfalls and the statistical testing of a backtest.

units.title: Linear regression: OLS, geometry and interpretation
objectives: Estimate OLS slope and intercept by hand for a small sample
Interpret coefficients, R-squared and residuals; link to projection (Q6)
State the Gauss-Markov assumptions and what each buys
units.worked_example: Fund returns vs market for 6 months give slope (beta) = 0.92 and alpha = 0.10%/month: a CAPM regression read off in 3 lines.

exercises.task: Compute beta and alpha from small data table
R^2 from SSR and SST
Which assumption failing biases OLS?
Fill in the matrix form of OLS

units.title: Inference, heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation-robust errors
objectives: Test coefficient hypotheses with t- and F-statistics

Compute a confidence interval and judge significance
units.worked_example: Estimated beta 1.1, standard error 0.40: t = 2.75; with Newey-West the se becomes 0.65, t = 1.7, no longer significant at 5%.

exercises.task: t-statistic and 95% CI
What do HAC standard errors correct?
Sort diagnostics (Durbin-Watson, Breusch-Pagan, White) by problem
Spot the misinterpretation of a regression table in a research note

units.title: Time series: stationarity, ARMA and forecasting
objectives: Test by reasoning whether an AR(1) is stationary and compute its moments
Interpret ACF/PACF pictures to choose AR vs MA
Produce multi-step AR(1) forecasts and show mean reversion
units.worked_example: AR(1) with phi = 0.8, mean 2%: shock of +1% today forecasts +0.8% tomorrow, +0.51% in 3 days; unconditional variance = sigma^2/(1-0.64).

exercises.task: AR(1) k-step forecast and variance
Match ACF/PACF patterns to AR/MA orders
Is a process with |phi| = 1.0 stationary?
Unconditional variance of an AR(1)

units.title: Unit roots, spurious regression and cointegration
objectives: Distinguish trend-stationary and unit-root processes and apply the Dickey-Fuller logic
Explain why regressing two independent random walks gives spurious results
Describe cointegration and its use in pairs / basis relationships
units.worked_example: Two independent random walks regressed on each other show R^2 = 0.6 and t = 12: spurious; but an ETF and its NAV differ by a stationary spread (P5 callback), so they are cointegrated.

exercises.task: Which regression signature suggests spuriousness?
Sort series as I(0) or I(1): returns, prices, spreads, rates
Order the Engle-Granger two-step procedure
Dickey-Fuller t-statistic and decision at critical value -2.86

units.title: Volatility stylised facts and ARCH
objectives: List stylised facts of returns: fat tails, clustering, leverage effect
Compute conditional variance from an ARCH(1) recursion
Test (conceptually) for ARCH effects
units.worked_example: ARCH(1) with omega = 0.00002, alpha = 0.3: after a -3% return the next-day variance is 0.00002 + 0.3 x 0.0009 = 0.00029, i.e., vol 1.70%.

exercises.task: ARCH(1) conditional variance from last return
Unconditional variance omega/(1-alpha)
Which stylised fact does the normal distribution contradict?
Sort return facts into 'explained by ARCH' vs 'not explained'

units.title: GARCH family, forecasting volatility and VaR
objectives: Run a GARCH(1,1) recursion and forecast variance over a horizon
Explain persistence, half-life and why GARCH mean-reverts to long-run variance
Compute parametric VaR from a conditional variance forecast and explain EGARCH/GJR asymmetry
units.worked_example: omega = 0.000002, alpha = 0.08, beta = 0.90: long-run variance 0.0001 (vol 1.0%/day); persistence 0.98, half-life ln 0.5/ln 0.98 = 34 days.

exercises.task: One-step GARCH(1,1) variance update
exercises.params: omega, alpha, beta, last return, last variance

exercises.task: Half-life of variance shocks
1-day 99% VaR on a portfolio from forecast vol

Spot the problem in a VaR report that uses constant vol after a shock

units.title: Research design: events, overfitting, multiple testing and backtests
objectives: Design an event study and compute a cumulative abnormal return
Explain data snooping, look-ahead and survivorship bias with examples from fund and index data
Adjust significance for multiple tests (Bonferroni idea) and judge a backtest claim
units.worked_example: A strategy picked as best of 40 variants shows t = 2.4; with Bonferroni the threshold for 5% overall is about t = 3.0, so the claim fails.

exercises.task: Cumulative abnormal return for a 5-day window
Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold
Spot the bias in a fund-performance table (dead funds missing)
Optional: critique a published-style backtest summary

modules.unit_test: OLS inference, ARMA, unit roots, GARCH, event-study and multiple-testing judgement.

modules.title: Measure-theoretic probability & analysis bridge
modules.hook: Sigma-algebras, measures, the Lebesgue integral, and the convergence theorems used in stochastic-calculus proofs, introduced through finite examples.

units.title: Why measure theory: sets, sigma-algebras and probability spaces
objectives: Verify whether a collection of sets is a sigma-algebra
Describe a probability space and information as a sigma-algebra (filtration idea)
Explain why not every subset of [0,1] can be given a length
units.worked_example: Coin tossed twice: F_1 = information after toss 1 has 4 sets; F_2 is all 16 subsets; a filtration is the growing sequence.

exercises.task: Which collections are sigma-algebras?
Count events in the sigma-algebra generated by a partition
Fill in the axioms of a probability measure
Sort events by F_0, F_1, F_2 measurability

units.title: Random variables, distributions and modes of convergence
objectives: Check measurability of a function and compute the law of a random variable
Distinguish almost-sure, in probability, in L^p and in distribution convergence
Give a counterexample separating two modes
key_concepts: a.s. vs in probability vs L^2 vs weak convergence
convergence of Riemann sums vs Itô sums
units.worked_example: X_n = n on a set of probability 1/n and 0 elsewhere: X_n -> 0 in probability but E|X_n| = 1 does not go to 0.

exercises.task: Match each convergence mode to its definition
Which implication holds (a.s. => in probability, converse false)?
Check convergence in probability numerically for given P(|X_n|>eps)
Spot the invalid step in a proof sketch that exchanges limit and expectation

units.title: Lebesgue integral, expectation and limit theorems
objectives: Describe the Lebesgue integral as expectation, via simple functions
State and apply monotone and dominated convergence
Explain when E[lim] = lim E[] fails
units.worked_example: X_n = n 1_{(0,1/n)} on [0,1]: pointwise limit 0 but E[X_n] = 1: no dominating integrable function, so DCT is not available.

exercises.task: Which theorem justifies exchanging limit and integral here?
Expectation of a simple random variable
Fill in the DCT hypothesis
Spot the illegal interchange in a pricing derivation (option payoff limit)

units.title: Conditional expectation as a projection
objectives: Compute E[X | G] for a finite partition
State tower, 'taking out what is known' and Jensen properties
Interpret conditional expectation as least-squares best predictor given information

exercises.task: E[X | partition cell] on a finite space
Fill the conditional expectation tree for a 3-step process

objectives: Verify martingale property for a given process

units.worked_example: Fair-coin walk starting at 3, stopped at 0 or 10: P(reaches 10) = 3/10 by optional stopping on a martingale S_n.

exercises.task: Which processes are martingales?

units.title: Radon-Nikodym, change of measure and a glance at rigorous stochastic calculus
objectives: Compute a likelihood ratio dQ/dP on a finite space and re-weight an expectation
State Girsanov in measure-theoretic form and explain why Q and P are equivalent

units.worked_example: Binomial P(up) = 0.6, Q(up) = 0.4: Z = 4/6 on up, 6/4 on down; E_P[Z] = 1 and E_Q[X] = E_P[Z X].

modules.title: Numerical methods (concepts, no coding)
modules.hook: Monte Carlo, finite-difference and tree methods for path-dependent products: method selection, test design and the checking of model output.

units.title: Monte Carlo: the idea, its error and its limits
objectives: Describe the Monte Carlo estimator for a discounted expectation and its standard error
Compute the number of paths needed for a target accuracy
Explain the 1/sqrt(N) rate and when MC is preferred
units.worked_example: Payoff sd 12 EUR, wanted standard error 0.01 EUR: N = (12/0.01)^2 = 1.44 million paths; halving the error needs four times more.

exercises.task: Required paths for a target standard error
Confidence interval for an MC price estimate
Which product features favour Monte Carlo over trees/PDE?
Sort problems into 'MC natural' vs 'PDE natural'

units.title: Variance reduction, Greeks by simulation and American options
objectives: Explain antithetic variates, control variates and importance sampling in words
Compare pathwise, likelihood-ratio and bump-and-revalue Greek estimators
Describe Longstaff-Schwartz regression for early exercise
units.worked_example: Pricing an arithmetic Asian with the geometric Asian (closed form) as control variate cuts variance by roughly 95% at same path count.

exercises.task: Match each technique to its mechanism
Variance reduction factor 1 - rho^2 with control variate

units.title: Finite differences for the Black-Scholes PDE
objectives: Describe a grid in (S, t) and the explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson schemes
Explain stability and why explicit schemes need small time steps
Set boundary and terminal conditions for calls, puts and barriers
units.worked_example: Explicit scheme with dS = 1 and sigma = 25% at S = 100: stability needs dt <= dS^2/(sigma^2 S^2) = 0.0016 years, about 0.4 trading days; implicit has no such restriction.

exercises.task: Match schemes to stability and accuracy properties
Maximum stable time step for explicit scheme
Place boundary conditions at S=0 and S large for call/put
Why is Crank-Nicolson second-order accurate in time?

units.title: Trees, method choice, convergence and model risk

exercises.task: Fill in the method choice matrix for six products

modules.title: Behavioural finance

units.title: Prospect theory and the standard biases
objectives: Compute prospect value with value function and loss aversion
Explain probability weighting and why small probabilities are over-weighted
Identify overconfidence, anchoring and mental accounting in case descriptions
units.worked_example: Gain of 100 vs loss of 100 with 50/50 odds and lambda = 2: value = 0.5 x 100^0.88 - 0.5 x 2 x 100^0.88 < 0, so the bet is refused although expected value is 0.

exercises.task: Prospect value of a gamble

units.title: Limits to arbitrage, sentiment and market anomalies
